findings.evidence: The memo calls for one F0 fold/seed reconstruction with fixed archived weights, same-row comparison, and component-paired uncertainty, and explicitly says this cannot estimate public score, establish a winner, or satisfy the 30-cell general-comparison requirement. It forbids tuning blend weights to the public score and separates the clean F0 analogue from production fit scope.
findings.title: The proposed comparison is appropriately scoped

findings.evidence: The plan requires F0 exclusion from each member, warm initializer, teacher, teacher-target cache, propensity/calibration object, and learned preprocessing. It requires source/config/checkpoint/target-cache closure and says to stop if orgbase or any ancestor cannot be proven clean; it does not silently drop teachers or relabel full-fit checkpoints.
findings.title: The clean-fit gate accounts for learned ancestry

findings.evidence: The transcript binding identifies user-transcribed submission 1lmehfi3 / tl3.zip / displayed score 0.66832. Its local/server inventory entry lists the 0.34 distilled-s5, 0.33 tied-lead-s5, and 0.33 tied-lead-s6 recipe. CONTROL_ASSET_MAP records those production runs as train+valid, include_heldout_valid=true, valid_fold=-1 and marks them ineligible as local clean controls. The model catalog supports the stated 211/263 feature counts, GRU/tied-lead families, and optimizer/EMA distinctions. The membership receipt supports equal ordered old/canonical fit and evaluation memberships (10,535 fit.train, 1,405 fit.valid, 468 evaluation.valid) while requiring preservation of distinct split identities.
findings.title: Member recipe and membership details match the bound metadata

findings.evidence: The memo repeats the map’s uncertified status and the sibling recipe’s different teachers and 467/10,606/1,406 split counts, and treats those runs only as context rather than as substitutes for the tl3 recipe.
findings.title: Nearest historical siblings are not misrepresented as exact counterparts

findings.evidence: The public trace binds the displayed public ID/filename/score from user transcription to the local/server archive by filename only; portal_payload_sha256 and actual_portal_payload_sha256 are null. The plan states this caveat in its opening paragraph, but phrases such as “Its fixed members are” and the closing “The public tl3 package is a final train+valid fit” can still imply that the uploaded ZIP’s contents and training scope have been proven.
findings.recommended_action: When using the memo as a factual summary, say “the inventoried local tl3 archive’s fixed members” and “the inventoried production members are train+valid fits”; retain the explicit statement that portal-uploaded bytes are unverified. This is a wording clarification, not a blocker to the proposed clean reconstruction.
findings.title: Qualify statements about the public package recipe

limits: The trace supports the public ID, filename, displayed score, and local/server archive inventory binding, but does not prove portal-upload bytes equal the archived ZIP.

The asset map is bounded metadata evidence: it explicitly says checkpoint/target payloads were not rehashed or replayed and some teacher/cache/propensity ancestry remains uncertified. The plan correctly treats those as pre-launch closure gates.
This review assesses the proposed experiment only; it does not validate a future reconstructed run or its metric.
scope: Read-only scientific-adequacy and claim-boundary review of the TL3 clean-counterpart plan against the public submission trace, its independent review/binding, CONTROL_ASSET_MAP, F0 membership receipt, and model catalog. No model or array access, training, fitting, remote action, or tests.
